about.title: Tracy Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Tracy takes many shapes. Some people spend their shifts in buildings and yards near I-205; others drive routes along Grant Line Road, Corral Hollow Road, and 11th Street; still others frame houses, stock shelves, or care for patients across San Joaquin County. When a shift ends in an injury, the path forward is not always obvious. Under California law, workers' compensation is usually your only claim against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. If someone outside your company contributed to the harm, though, the picture changes. A subcontractor on the same site, the owner of the property where you were working, the maker of a tool that failed, or another driver who hit you while you were on the clock may each support a separate personal injury claim alongside your comp benefits. Tracy recorded 221 injury collisions in 2025, and a portion of any city's crashes involve people doing their jobs. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Tracy Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Systems, One Conversation
items.desc: Workers' comp is generally your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party can still be held responsible in a separate claim. An attorney from our network can look at both at once so nothing is left on the table.

items.title: Deadlines That Do Not Wait
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party injury claim generally carries a two-year filing window. Reaching out early keeps both clocks from becoming a problem.

items.title: Protection Against Pushback
items.desc: It is illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a comp claim. If you are worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your rights before you speak up.

items.question: I was hit on I-205 while driving a company vehicle. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, your medical care and part of your wages would typically run through workers' compensation, no matter who caused the crash. If another driver was at fault, you may also bring a separate personal injury claim against that driver. An attorney can coordinate the two so they do not work against each other.

items.question: Do I have to report a Tracy work injury right away?
items.answer: California asks you to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury or of learning it was work-related. Reporting in writing and keeping a copy is a simple way to protect yourself. Waiting longer can complicate your benefits, so it is better to report even if you are unsure how serious the injury is.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a claim?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or pursuing workers' compensation is against California law. If you have been demoted, cut back, or let go after reporting, tell the attorney you are connected with, because that may be a separate issue worth addressing.
